runs.text: The Human Fiction is a philosophical and reflective work.
It is not intended to provide psychological, medical, legal, or professional advice of any kind.
All ideas presented in this book are part of an interpretive framework exploring perception, identity, memory, and narrative construction.
They are meant for contemplation, not instruction.
Any resemblance between the concepts described and personal experiences of the reader is a natural reflection of shared human cognition patterns, not a claim of universal truth.
The content does not aim to define reality, but to examine how reality is interpreted through thought.
Readers are encouraged to engage with the material critically and independently.
No interpretation within this book should be treated as absolute or final.
The author holds no responsibility for personal interpretations, emotional responses, or decisions arising from the reading of this material.
This work is not a replacement for professional guidance in any domain.
It is a literary and philosophical exploration of human perception itself.
